chapter.title: Start-up
chapter.para: These requirements cover what JetOS does between the moment a boot loader or the firmware hands over the module and the moment the first partition runs.

section.title: SRQ_JET_BOOT_001
section.para: JetOS shall start on x86_64 when it is loaded by a Multiboot boot loader, and on arm64 when it is entered at exception level 1 or 2.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: These are the ways in which QEMU, the target of both boards, starts a kernel image.

section.title: SRQ_JET_BOOT_002
section.para: JetOS shall initialize, before the first partition runs: the processor, the board (the consoles, the interrupt controller, the timer and the calendar clock), the memory spaces of the partitions, the partitions, the channels between ports and the schedule, in an order in which each step finds what it needs ready.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The partitions can be started only on top of memory protection, a clock and a console.

section.title: SRQ_JET_BOOT_003
section.para: JetOS shall start the consoles first, so that an error found during the rest of the start-up can be reported.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Nothing else is available to show why a module does not come up.

section.title: SRQ_JET_BOOT_004
section.para: JetOS shall start the schedule at the first slot of a major frame at the end of its initialization, and its start-up code shall not return.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The module runs the partitions for as long as it is powered; there is nothing to return to.

section.title: SRQ_JET_BOOT_005
section.para: JetOS shall report a fatal error found during start-up (for example an invalid memory block) on the main console and shall then stop the module.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Health monitoring needs partitions, which do not exist yet at that point.

section.title: SRQ_JET_BOOT_006
section.para: JetOS shall run the application's main function directly, with no partitions, when it is built for a module with no partitions configured.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The kernel started as a single-program operating system before it became a partitioning one; this behaviour is kept for the examples that use it.
